Research notes

01 /Market structureWhat a listed BDC basket can—and cannot—tell us.+

A proxy with boundaries

Listed business development companies connect private lending to public equity markets. Their share prices reflect leverage, distributions, discount rates, and investor sentiment as well as credit fundamentals. This basket therefore measures a public-market proxy, not private loan marks or private-credit default rates.

The index compounds equal-weight daily constituent returns over the common observation window. The original implementation averaged share prices, giving higher-priced shares more influence. The revised calculation eliminates that distortion. Macro observations from the legacy database are excluded because their provenance cannot be verified.

02 /Loan-level riskHonest validation starts with information available before the outcome.+

Predicting a synthetic outcome

A chronological origination-cohort split reserves later loans for evaluation. Imputation, scaling, and category encoding fit only on training data. The allowlist excludes supplied PD, expected loss, recoveries, survival duration, and other outcome-related or derived fields.

Both prespecified models are reported without selecting a winner on the holdout. The target covers varied loan lifetimes; a classifier score is not an annual default forecast. The stress illustration separately uses the dataset’s supplied annual PD and LGD. Synthetic performance is an engineering demonstration, not evidence of investment skill.

03 /Liquidity mechanicsA redemption gate buys time. A haircut consumes capital.+

The cash has to come from somewhere

To pay a redemption of 10 at an 85% realization price, a fund must sell 11.76 of book assets, recognizing a loss of 1.76. The simulator limits each payment by the initial-NAV gate, outstanding requests, and available sale proceeds. It stops when requests are fulfilled or assets are exhausted.

This is a deliberately small, auditable model: one redemption cohort, no existing cash, no debt, no income, and no new requests. Gates are applied to initial NAV. It does not reproduce any particular fund’s terms.

Evidence, before conclusions.

This portfolio brings together two independent research projects and an accounting-based liquidity experiment. It makes the evidence status of each explicit.

01 / Market snapshot

Provenance is unverified. The archived macro series may be simulated and is not used. No current market claims or verified investment returns are presented.

02 / Synthetic loan experiment

Logistic regression and random forest use identical training and holdout partitions. AUC intervals use 200 fixed-seed bootstrap resamples. Lower Brier score indicates smaller squared probability error. Original dataset attribution and redistribution rights were not recorded; the public export includes aggregates, not raw loans.

03 / Liquidity accounting

Assets sold = redemption paid ÷ realization price. Haircut loss = assets sold − redemption paid. Gate = a fixed fraction of initial NAV per quarter. All amounts are normalized to initial NAV of 100.
